Recently, out of the blue my account is blocked. To unblock, it prompts me to check the ‘I’m not a robot’ box saying it will then redirect me to the unblocking page, but it never does. It again returns to the same page where it asked me for recaptcha. It’s a glitched loop, and I’m not even able to access my account anymore.
Complaining on Truecaller customer support has yielded no result as they haven’t got back to me in the stipulated 48 hours. 
All I can say is, this app is disgusting and disappointing.

reviews.title: A Decade of Loyalty, Then This
reviews.text: I’ve used Truecaller for 10 years, and this change is incredibly disappointing. Features I relied on for years are now locked behind a $74.99/year Premium subscription. I already had the app installed and all caller identification settings enabled, but I was still being pushed into a paywall just to continue using functionality I previously had access to. That is not an improvement; it’s a downgrade for longtime users. After a decade of using Truecaller, I deleted the app entirely, which says a lot about how poorly this change has been handled.

Secondly, I received some spam calls which I managed to block but it turns out that the spam numbers weren't added to my block list. Finally, I thought I'd contact support and explained what was happening as I really wanted this app to work. I received an auto-reply email immediately with the promise that somebody would contact me within 48 hours - 6 days later and not a word from them. I'm pleased this has all happened during my trial and I certainly won't be continuing with the Family plan.

reviews.title: Caused More Harm Than Good
reviews.text:
The AI functionality (where an AI assistant answers calls to screen out spam) is terrible and actually resulted in me getting more spam calls.  For starters, it cannot even say a realistic, normal “hello” and bizarrely identifies itself to every caller it speaks to as the “tele-phony assistant.”  The worse part is that, despite it understanding a caller to ask for my age (to see if I’m elderly) or asking if I have Medicare Parts A and B, it tells each caller to please hold while it checks with me, rather than automatically flagging the call as spam and blocking the number.  I discovered that whenever it asked a spam robocall bot to please hold, the bot would respond by saying it would call back.  As a result, I ended up receiving more spam calls with this app than without it.  I simply have no idea what the developers of this app were thinking.

Additionally, the app claims to have the functionality to block all numbers with a certain prefix specified by the user.  This would have been very helpful, but I found this function simply did not work.  And even had it worked, users are limited to a total of just five prefix blocks.

CNAP (Calling Name Presentation) will be enforced across India by March 2026, according to the Department of Telecommunications (DoT).

---

📅 Enforcement Timeline

• Pilot Phase (Late 2025): Telecom operators like Jio, Airtel, and BSNL are currently running pilot implementations in select circles.
• Pan-India Rollout Deadline: The DoT has directed all telecom service providers to make CNAP available nationwide by March 2026 The India... +1.
• TRAI’s Role: TRAI had earlier recommended CNAP in February 2024, and DoT confirmed the rollout plan in September 2025 Telecom Regu....


---

⚙️ How It Will Be Rolled Out

• Initial Devices: CNAP will first be supported on 5G devices and compatible 4G smartphones Business Sta....
• Default Setting: TRAI has suggested a default opt-out model, meaning CNAP will be enabled automatically unless users choose to disable it.
• Business Numbers: Operators are working on clarifications for shared or enterprise numbers, where attribution of the caller name may be complex Business Sta....


---

🔑 Why This Matters

• Verified Caller Identity: CNAP will display the official KYC name of the caller, unlike Truecaller which relies on crowdsourced data.
• Spam & Fraud Reduction: By showing government-verified names, CNAP will make it harder for fraudsters to spoof identities.
• Privacy Protection: Data stays within telecom operators and government frameworks, avoiding third-party data harvesting.

We made you what you are today. We helped you build your database for FREE. We didn’t charge you.
First you imposed skip able ads on us, then you impose ads that can’t be skipped and now you’ve made number searches chargeable? This is ridiculous. Basic search database that we helped you build, now you are charging us to view that? Nobody will pay for this. You can’t keep backing users into a corner like that testing their limits.
I suggest everyone to not give this app access to your contacts and do not report or block numbers on this app. Instead block the numbers directly on your phone. Do not give this app any help or data anymore.

reviews.title: Pathetic App
reviews.text: The app asks to access your contacts which basically form their database to perform caller ID search. And in return, they are trying every bit to make you subscribe them. If I am allowing them to access my contacts and contribute to their database (which forms the backbone of their operation), they should at least allow me to look for caller IDs even if is in return of watching an advertisement. Their frustration with non-subscriptions has gone to such a level that they have  limited the number of searches per day for a user (even in return of watching an advertisement which is allowing them with a revenue stream). While this app is not a social service and needs money to operate, using customers’ contacts to support their database without offering them any significant value is not justified and a probable gateway to losing the success / popularity they achieved in recent years. Not recommending  this app with their current business model.
